_note: Planning doc — Phase 1 detail. NOT a live entity. See ../campaign_arc.json for the big picture this breaks down from.
name: Something is Happening
goal: The party learns that incidents at the Academy are escalating and begins to uncover why — the existence of the veil, its history, and its current instability.

inciting_hook.description: The party overhears Ambrose Quill and Captain Hadra (both existing NPCs) talking. It's a casual conversation between two friends, not a clandestine meeting — Ambrose is gossipy and does most of the talking. The conversation reveals that the frequency of 'incidents' at the Academy has been increasing over the last several years.
inciting_hook.tone: Casual, gossipy — the party is eavesdropping on an ordinary chat, not uncovering a secret briefing.
inciting_hook.npc_suspicion: Ambrose and Hadra suspect there's a single underlying source behind the pattern, but don't know what or who it is.

incidents_mentioned.count: Three incidents, all within the current school year.

dinosaur_infiltration.description: Students were almost killed by a dinosaur infiltration during a standard midterm exercise.
dinosaur_infiltration.cause: A magical item was unknowingly planted in the catalog for use with the midterms — the item attracts dinosaurs and makes them rage.
dinosaur_infiltration.placeholder: Identity of the item, and who/what planted it, not yet decided.

tainted_component_pouch.description: An incident in the Arcane Tower's shared component stores — used by both Wizards and Sorcerers students. A tainted component pouch, marked underneath with a small Thornwick Arcane Consortium stamp, caused a bad incident when its contents were used. Wizards and Sorcerers blamed each other; neither department was actually responsible.
tainted_component_pouch.cause: The pouch itself, planted among the shared supplies — origin/planter not yet decided.

angry_instrument.description: A single instrument, left anonymously in the Bards Department's instrument storage closet. Enchanted to build anger in whoever plays it past a few minutes. Discovered because a rehearsal nearly ended in a fistfight over nothing.
angry_instrument.cause: The instrument itself, left anonymously — origin/planter not yet decided.

details.founders_persona_constraint: See campaign_arc.json continuity_notes.founders_persona_rewrite — the founders are being written as well-intentioned. No Phase 1 clue should imply otherwise.

confirmed.name: The Founders' Correspondence
confirmed.description: A hidden chest in an old storage room contains newly discovered correspondence between founding members. Among it, a cryptic letter that, once deciphered, mentions the veil and one founder's concern that more protections are needed.
confirmed.status: confirmed — needs a specific storage room location and the deciphering method worked out

confirmed.name: Voss's Notes
confirmed.description: The party finds notes belonging to Dr. Ellery Voss. They are actually Ninth Thesis investigation materials — Voss runs the Ninth Thesis (see the_ninth_thesis.json), an organization that hunts hidden evil and is already investigating the source of the incidents. Whether Voss left the notes findable by accident or on purpose is left ambiguous, leaning toward intentional — this ties Voss to the organization and ties its investigation directly into the party's hook.
confirmed.draft_text:
[Scrawled across several loose pages, ink smudged in places — clearly not meant for anyone else to read]

Three this year. Three, this school year alone — not spread across some longer span I could talk myself out of.

- The catalog item — someone fed something into the midterm requisitions that had no business being there. Attracted the pack, and worse, angered them past anything natural. I've asked Provisions for the acquisition record twice. Twice I've been told it "doesn't exist." A requisition doesn't stop existing.
- The component pouch in the Arcane Tower stores. Wizards and Sorcerers share that supply room and spent a week blaming each other for what happened, which told me plainly that neither of them did it. Turned the pouch over myself after. Small mark stamped on the underside — Thornwick Arcane Consortium. I've seen that mark before and never once thought about where it came from.
- An instrument, left anonymous in the practice closet. Ordinary to look at. Enchanted to feed on its own sound — play it past a few minutes and whoever's holding it starts wanting to hurt something. Found because a rehearsal nearly ended in a fistfight over nothing.

The Academy's never been silent — I've read the incident logs back generations, and something goes wrong here every so often, has for centuries. That's not what stops me. What stops me is the shape of it. The old incidents are scattered — years apart, no common thread, easy enough to write off one at a time as bad luck. These three are not that. Three, inside a single year, and every one of them traces back to something that shouldn't have been where it was — placed there, not natural. That's not the campus's old checkered luck repeating. That's a pattern, close together and all the same shape, and patterns have authors.

"A secret, once it is understood for what it is, is a kind of power." I keep coming back to that line. Read it again last night. She wasn't writing about ghosts or thieves. She meant something living here, wearing the ordinary shape of the place, using its silence as cover.

If she was right — and I think she was — then something is doing exactly that. Somewhere on these grounds. I don't know what. I don't know where. I have three incidents, one old thesis, and a very bad feeling that we've been standing on top of something for three hundred and fifty years and calling it a floor.

Need more before I bring this to anyone. Cross-reference incident dates against the exam schedule and faculty travel logs. Start with Provisions — someone signed for that catalog entry.

— E.V.
confirmed.draft_text_status: Draft — all three incidents now specified and explicitly placed within the current school year; note emphasizes recency/consistency (same 'planted item' shape) against an acknowledged but scattered/random older incident history. Yours to revise or approve.
confirmed.status: concept + draft text done; where/how the party finds them, and how deliberate Voss's 'carelessness' reads in the scene, still placeholder

confirmed.name: The Memorial Garden Plaques
confirmed.description: A coded message split across the three founders' memorial plaques. Each founder's portion is a direct quotation attributed to them — their own words, not later commentary — so the clue speaks in their own voice.
confirmed.status: concept confirmed; actual plaque text, code/cipher method, and how the message is split across the three founders is still placeholder

rejected.name: Physical ritual-binding components (founders_charter / ritual_floor tie-in)
rejected.reason: Doesn't fit Brennan Ashcroft's updated well-intentioned persona — he would not have taken and lost a binding component.

rejected.name: voss_imprint triangulation clue
rejected.reason: Would let the party physically locate the veil before learning about the possessed former student in Phase 2, which needs to happen first.

clues.still_needed: Current set may be sufficient — TBD, more can be added later.

details.structural_constraint: Phase 1 clues should lead to discovering THAT the veil exists and why it's unstable, but should NOT let the party physically locate the veil itself — that's gated behind Phase 2 (learning about the one who got away).
details.end_condition: Phase 1 ends when the party makes the discovery and starts actively trying to locate the veil or dig up more information about it.
